exposure: Neonatal birth weight classification (appropriate/small for gestational age)
outcome: Successful vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC)
cohort: Women with singleton term pregnancies, one previous cesarean section, and a live fetus in cephalic presentation who delivered between January 2013 and December 2015.
finding: Factors associated with a higher likelihood of vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC) included a history of prior vaginal delivery, cervical dilation of at least 4 cm at admission, a Bishop score of 6 or higher, spontaneous onset of labor, absence of chronic hypertension, and lower neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: VBAC was more likely in women with cervical dilation of 4 cm or more at admission, a Bishop score of 6 or higher, a history of vaginal birth, spontaneous labor onset, absence of chronic hypertension, and lower neonatal birth weight.
birth_weight: Neonates classified as appropriate or small for gestational age; lower neonatal birth weight.
